title: Noor and the Deadline
premise: Gideon Iversen, a private security contractor who has spent years keeping clients off every record, discovers the safe house she runs has been listed for sale online — with interior photos that reveal her tradecraft, her routes, and her face. The listing is bait, and the defector she's been hiding inside it, a disgraced Frankfurt bank analyst named Elias Brandt, may be the lure meant to draw out the network that once employed Gideon. With markets opening in Frankfurt in seventy-two hours, she must move Brandt through a city that now knows exactly where to look for them. In the end, Gideon chooses truth over loyalty: she testifies anonymously against her former employer, trading her invisibility for justice, and walks away alive but permanently exposed.
about_author: A. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade advising firms on executive protection across Europe. They write thrillers about people whose jobs depend on never being seen.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Scrolling property sites at 3 a.m., Gideon finds the safe house listed with photos showing her go-bags, her camera angles, even a reflection of her in a hallway mirror. The emotional beat is cold vertigo — the realization that someone sold her invisibility deliberately, and that whoever did it wants her to know.

chapters.title: Asset Under Glass
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. She reviews the file on Elias Brandt, the defector sleeping one room away, and notices his handler's contact pattern matches the realtor's email domain. The beat is creeping suspicion: either Brandt is compromised, or he is the compromise — bait dressed as an asset.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. A burner call from her old employer, Corvane Group, offers extraction for Brandt 'before Frankfurt opens' — but demands she hand him over at a location visible from three directions. The beat is a trap tightening; Gideon accepts while planning not to comply.

chapters.title: What Brandt Knows
chapters.summary: POV: Brandt. The defector reveals he didn't flee with secrets — he fled because he refused to launder them, and Corvane's clients need him discredited before Monday. The beat is reluctant alliance: two people realizing they're pieces in the same board game.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. She stages the safe house for a fake viewing, feeding the watchers a scripted performance of panic and packing. The beat is controlled deception turning to dread when a viewer photographs a wall only Brandt could have described.

chapters.title: The Handler's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Breaking into her former handler's flat, she finds a ledger of sold identities — including her own, priced months ago. The beat is grief and fury: her erasure was always inventory, and someone she trusted signed the invoice.

chapters.title: Night Train South
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Gideon and Brandt. They move Brandt by rail under cover of a freight manifest, evading two separate surveillance teams. The beat is fragile trust hardening into loyalty — until Gideon admits aloud that Brandt might still be the bait, and he agrees to be used anyway.

chapters.title: Frankfurt, Before the Bell
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Ninety minutes before markets open, Gideon delivers Brandt to the exchange — but to journalists and a financial regulator, not to Corvane, broadcasting his testimony live. The beat is the point of no return: she burns every bridge, every alias, all at once.

chapters.title: Price of the Ticket
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Corvane's cleaners close in through the crowd; a brutal chase through the financial district ends with Gideon trading the ledger itself for passage out, letting the evidence surface without her name attached. The beat is costly survival — she lives, but nothing of her old life does.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon, epilogue voice. Weeks later, Corvane collapses under investigation and Brandt testifies safely abroad. Gideon, unmasked and unemployable in her old trade, sits in a café under her real name for the first time in nine years. The beat is quiet resolution: justice cost her everything except herself.
